_comment: Agent harness runtime characteristics. agents.json catalogs memory architectures; this file catalogs RUNTIMES — how the harness loops, manages context, persists state, integrates MCP. Overlap is intentional (Claude Code / Goose / Hermes / Letta appear in both, viewed differently).

harnesses.name: Claude Code
harnesses.verdict: ★ winner for personal corpus + MCP — first-class, plaintext state, predictable loop, paranoid permissions

harnesses.name: Goose
harnesses.mcp: first-class — reference impl for MCP spec, 70+ extensions
harnesses.verdict: ★ best fully-open option — multi-provider, MCP is reference-quality, fluid UX

harnesses.name: Hermes Agent
harnesses.loop: agentic + skill-building (learns / distills runs into reusable skills)
harnesses.context: lossy summarization + persistent memory blocks (in-context across evictions)
harnesses.state: SQLite FTS5 + skills DB + 8 external memory providers (Holographic/HRR, Honcho, Hindsight, Supermemory)
harnesses.models: model-agnostic; 200+ providers via LiteLLM (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM, OpenRouter)
harnesses.ui: CLI TUI + Hermes Desktop + Hermes Workspace + Telegram/Discord/Slack/Signal gateways
harnesses.verdict: ★★ memory-first — pick when you need cross-session learning, scheduled cron tasks, or HRR's algebraic composition

harnesses.name: Cursor
harnesses.loop: agent executor with parallel subagents (/multitask in v3.2)
harnesses.context: codebase indexing + semantic search; per-subagent windows
harnesses.models: multi-provider; Cursor cloud for cloud features
harnesses.verdict: skip for personal corpus — vendor lock, server-side state

harnesses.name: Cline
harnesses.loop: ReAct with sequential approval gates; read-only subagents
harnesses.verdict: skip — IDE-bound, permission gates become friction, subagents are read-only

harnesses.name: Continue.dev
harnesses.verdict: fine for coding-in-IDE, not the right shape for general corpus work

harnesses.name: Letta
harnesses.loop: agent loop with self-managed memory (agent writes own memory)
harnesses.mcp: second-class — native tool registry, MCP integration partial
harnesses.verdict: elegant memory architecture but over-engineered for personal corpus — better as a chatbot backend

harnesses.name: Open Interpreter
harnesses.loop: reactive: model → code gen → exec → error feedback → next
harnesses.verdict: skip — not a harness, no state, no MCP. Good for one-off code-exec tasks only

harnesses.name: Open WebUI
harnesses.loop: frontend only — agent logic delegated to backend
harnesses.state: chat history in WebUI; backend decides persistence
harnesses.models: Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic — depends on backend
harnesses.verdict: use as a UI for one of the above — not an agent runtime itself

harnesses.name: Aider
harnesses.loop: ReAct: model → file edits → lint/test → refine
harnesses.verdict: skip for corpus work — git/code-edit centric, MCP is community-experimental

verdict.for_personal_corpus_plus_mcp: Claude Code is the clear winner. Goose is the strong fully-open alternative. Hermes if memory-learning across sessions matters. Use Open WebUI as a frontend if you want a web UI on top. Skip the rest.
verdict.honest_take: All three top picks (Claude Code, Goose, Hermes) work fine for the use case. The differentiator is taste: Claude Code if you trust Anthropic's stack and want polish; Goose if you want full openness and multi-provider routing; Hermes if you want the agent to learn skills across sessions.
